name: Japan
summary: Asia's oldest major market: the Tokyo Stock Exchange traces its origins to 1878 and is now part of Japan Exchange Group (JPX). Shares trade in fixed lots of 100, with a lunch break and daily price limits. TOPIX and the Nikkei 225 are the headline indexes.

currency.name: Japanese yen
currency.note: For a euro investor, Japanese shares carry currency risk: moves of the yen against the euro change the value of holdings in euros (Category L).

source.title: FTSE Equity Country Classification Process, v3.5, October 2026, Appendix 3 (FTSE Russell, PDF)

exchanges.name: Tokyo Stock Exchange (Japan Exchange Group)
exchanges.founded: 15 May 1878 (Tokyo Stock Exchange Co., Ltd.); present form 1949
exchanges.hours: Morning session 09:00–11:30, afternoon session 12:30–15:30 (the close moved from 15:00 to 15:30 in November 2024).
exchanges.note: Japan does not use daylight saving time.

indexes.name: TOPIX (Tokyo Stock Price Index)
indexes.description: A free-float adjusted, market-capitalisation-weighted index covering an extensive part of the Japanese market. Base: 100 points on 4 January 1968. Calculated by JPX.

indexes.name: Nikkei 225
indexes.description: A price index of 225 stocks on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's Prime Market, calculated by Nikkei Inc. It ended 1989 at a record 38,915 and only closed above that again on 22 February 2024 (Category K).

regulators.name: Financial Services Agency (FSA)
regulators.role: Japan's financial regulator, which also oversees the tax-free NISA investment accounts framework.

settlement.note: Trades on Monday settle on Wednesday; trades on Friday settle the following Tuesday.

source.title: Guide to TSE trading methodology, 2024 edition (JPX, PDF)

rules.title: Trading unit of 100 shares
rules.text: All common stocks of listed domestic companies trade in units of 100 shares since 1 October 2018, so the minimum purchase is 100 × the share price.

rules.title: Daily price limits
rules.text: Each share can only move within a set range around the previous close in one day; for example, from a close of ¥1,000 the limits are ¥700 and ¥1,300. Limits can widen after two days at the limit.

taxes.glance: Residents: 20.315% on listed-share dividends and gains (15.315% national + 5% local); NISA accounts tax-free. Non-residents: 15.315% withholding on listed-share dividends (20.42% for 3%+ holders), reducible by treaty.

items.title: Residents
items.text: Dividends on listed shares are taxed at 15.315% (income tax incl. reconstruction surtax) plus 5% local tax; gains on listed shares likewise.

items.title: NISA
items.text: Residents aged 18 or over can invest up to ¥1.2 million a year (tsumitate) and ¥2.4 million (growth) tax-free, with a lifetime limit of ¥18 million.

items.title: Non-residents
items.text: Listed-share dividends paid to non-residents are generally subject to 15.315% withholding; 20.42% applies to holders of 3% or more. A tax treaty may reduce this.

items.title: For an Austrian investor
items.text: An Austrian bank can credit foreign withholding tax up to 15% of the dividend against Austrian KESt (Category Q).

sources.title: No.1330 配当金を受け取ったとき (National Tax Agency, in Japanese)
No.1535 NISA制度 (National Tax Agency, in Japanese)
No.12006 Tax on the income of an individual non-resident (National Tax Agency)

access: Some Austrian banks and brokers offer trading on the Tokyo Stock Exchange; note the 100-share minimum lot and yen conversion.
Indirectly, through funds or ETFs on TOPIX, the Nikkei 225 or Asian indexes (Category H).

history.text: Tokyo Stock Exchange Co., Ltd. is established on 15 May.
The Tokyo Stock Exchange in its present form is founded (opened 16 May).
The Nikkei 225 ends the year at a record 38,915 (Category K).
The Nikkei 225 finally closes above its 1989 high (22 February); TSE's afternoon close moves to 15:30 (November).

sources.title: Japan's Nikkei closes above 1989's all-time high (Nikkei Asia)
